data.why: Vizarr is a purely client-side viewer that fetches OME-Zarr data directly from a remote URL given via the ?source query parameter; the README's own IDR example is small enough (pyramidal, range-requested) to use as-is and needs no local files.

goals: Open a multichannel OME-Zarr image by pasting its store URL into the ?source parameter
Toggle individual channels on and off to isolate structures of interest
Recolor channels to build an informative composite overlay
Adjust per-channel contrast limits to reveal dim or saturated signal
Step through z-slices and timepoints in a multiscale, multidimensional image
Pan and zoom across resolution pyramid levels to inspect fine detail without re-downloading the full-resolution image

review.summary: This is a careful, well-evidenced tree of single-image, multichannel Z-stack viewing in vizarr: every replayed task held up, the eight screens I checked match their nodes, and the levels are mostly right. Before filing, it needs the replay's corrections folded into the feature notes, a feature for opening an image from a link, and the label-overlay and multi-image or plate features (in the code but missing from the tree) recorded as not reached.
